rationale: Proofs C and E are fully correct and elementary: A minimizes m(w)-tw on [a,1], B minimizes m(w)-qw on [c,1], and the bound B<2A follows from comparing h(B)>=h(A) with g(B)<=g(c). C is best because it states the idea up front, labels each step (choice of A, choice of B, B near A), justifies A in (0,1) and B in (A,1), and notes that only continuity of m is used. E is equally correct and tighter but gives less orientation. B is correct and justifies the Lipschitz property of F and the closedness of contact points, but the differentiation-based route is heavier and less explanatory than the direct minimizer construction. A and D follow the same route with key claims (Lipschitz and monotonicity of F, local constancy, existence of nearby contacts) only asserted. D is the thinnest, with an unjustified Lipschitz sketch and no overview, so the reader must fill gaps.
